blocks.prompt: 6 Prove that: \(\dfrac{\sin 3\theta}{1 + 2\cos 2\theta} = \sin\theta\); deduce the value of \(\sin 15^{\circ}\).
blocks.explanation:
Two tasks: prove an identity, then use it for one special angle.
The key idea: \(\sin 3\theta\) can be split as \(\sin\theta + (\sin 3\theta - \sin\theta)\), and the bracket is a "sin − sin" that gives \(2\cos 2\theta\sin\theta\).
Plan: show \(\sin 3\theta = \sin\theta(1 + 2\cos 2\theta)\), divide, then put \(\theta = 15^{\circ}\) and rationalise.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin 3\theta}{1 + 2\cos 2\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \sin\theta\); then find \(\sin 15^{\circ}\).
Method: \(\sin P - \sin Q = 2\cos\frac{P + Q}{2}\sin\frac{P - Q}{2}\) to factorise the numerator.

Split the numerator
\[\sin 3\theta = \sin\theta + (\sin 3\theta - \sin\theta)\]
Why: Adding and subtracting \(\sin\theta\) changes nothing, but creates a difference of sines.

Change the bracket into a product
\[\sin 3\theta - \sin\theta = 2\cos 2\theta\sin\theta\]
Why: Half-sum \(\frac{4\theta}{2} = 2\theta\), half-difference \(\frac{2\theta}{2} = \theta\).

Factorise
\[\sin 3\theta = \sin\theta + 2\cos 2\theta\sin\theta\]
\[= \sin\theta(1 + 2\cos 2\theta)\]
Why: \(\sin\theta\) is common to both terms.

Divide
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{\sin\theta(1 + 2\cos 2\theta)}{1 + 2\cos 2\theta}\]
\[= \sin\theta = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: The bracket cancels (we need \(1 + 2\cos 2\theta \ne 0\)).

Deduction: put \(\theta = 15^{\circ}\)
\[\sin 15^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sin 45^{\circ}}{1 + 2\cos 30^{\circ}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{1 + 2\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}(1 + \sqrt{3})}\]
Why: \(3\theta = 45^{\circ}\) and \(2\theta = 30^{\circ}\) are angles whose values we know.

Rationalise the denominator
\[\sin 15^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{3} + 1)(\sqrt{3} - 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{2}(3 - 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2\sqrt{2}}\]
Why: Multiply top and bottom by \(\sqrt{3} - 1\); \((a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2\) removes the surd.

Check
\[\dfrac{1.7321 - 1}{2.8284} \approx 0.2588\]
\[\sin 15^{\circ} \approx 0.2588 \;\checkmark\]
Why: This also agrees with \(\sin 15^{\circ} = \sin(45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ})\) from Exercise 10.2.
